Stone of Jacob appears in Book of Genesis as stone used as pillow by Israelite patriarch Jacob at place later called Bet-El. Jacob had vision in sleep, consecrated stone to God. More recently, stone has been claimed by Scottish folklore and British Israelism.

Biblical narrative

According to account given in Genesis (Chapter 28:10-22), Jacob was fleeing elder twin brother Esau, whom he had cheated out of receiving father Isaac's blessing of first-born. Jacob rested at city called Luz, used stones as pillow, dreamed ladder set up on earth reached to heaven, angels of God ascending and descending on it. Lord said, I am Lord God of Abraham thy father, and God of Isaac: land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed; thy seed shall be as dust of earth; in thee and in thy seed shall all families of earth be blessed; I am with thee, will keep thee, bring thee again into this land, not leave thee.

After waking up, Jacob exclaimed, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but house of God, and this is gate of heaven. He called place Bethel, which translates to House of God.
